t: Temporal Fact Resolver: a plain-language overview
title: Temporal Fact Resolver: a plain-language overview
description: Overview: what the Temporal Fact Resolver does and why archives need it. A temporal fact resolver keeps history straight: it records not just what is true, but when it was true. 'She was CEO from 2018 to 2022' becomes a fact with a start date and an end date. When facts from different years disagree, the resolver lines them up on a timeline instead of letting them fight.
demo:
# Temporal Fact Resolver - runnable demo (JAH-ATK179-000001)
RANK = 1
SIG = False
FACTS = [('CEO: A. Rivera', 2018, 2022), ('CEO: J. Park', 2022, None), ('CTO: L. Chen', 2019, 2023)]  # (fact, start_year, end_year or None)
def allen(a, b):
    (s1, e1), (s2, e2) = a, b
    e1 = e1 or 9999; e2 = e2 or 9999
    if e1 < s2: return "before"
    if e1 == s2: return "meets"
    if s1 < s2 < e1 < e2: return "overlaps"
    if s2 <= s1 and e1 <= e2 and (s1, e1) != (s2, e2): return "during"
    if (s1, e1) == (s2, e2): return "equals"
    if s1 == s2: return "starts"
    return "related"
print("facts on the timeline:")
for f, s, e in FACTS:
    print("  [%s-%s] %s" % (s, e or "now", f))
if RANK >= 2:
    print("interval relations:")
    for i in range(len(FACTS)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(FACTS)):
            print("  '%s' %s '%s'" % (FACTS[i][0][:25], allen(FACTS[i][1:], FACTS[j][1:]), FACTS[j][0][:25]))
if RANK >= 3:
    q = 2020
    holder = [f for f, s, e in FACTS if s <= q <= (e or 9999)]
    print("true in %d: %s" % (q, holder if holder else "nothing recorded"))
if SIG:
    print("Signature lineage stamp: JAH-SIG-TMP-" + "JAH-ATK179-000001")
print("record:", "JAH-ATK179-000001", "OK")

t: How the Temporal Fact Resolver works
title: How the Temporal Fact Resolver works
description: Overview: what the Temporal Fact Resolver does and why archives need it. Real resolvers extract temporal expressions with parsers like SUTime or HeidelTime, normalize them to dates, and attach validity intervals [start, end) to every fact. Allen's interval algebra — thirteen relations including before, meets, overlaps, during, and equals — classifies how any two intervals relate, which detects contradictions (two CEOs 'during' the same month) and supports point-in-time queries ('who was CEO on 2020-06-01?'). t: How the Temporal Fact Resolver works: the deep tour
title: How the Temporal Fact Resolver works: the deep tour
description: Overview: what the Temporal Fact Resolver does and why archives need it. Real resolvers extract temporal expressions with parsers like SUTime or HeidelTime, normalize them to dates, and attach validity intervals [start, end) to every fact. Allen's interval algebra — thirteen relations including before, meets, overlaps, during, and equals — classifies how any two intervals relate, which detects contradictions (two CEOs 'during' the same month) and supports point-in-time queries ('who was CEO on 2020-06-01?'). Bitemporal models track both when something was true and when the archive learned it. Advanced systems handle fuzzy dates ('early 1990s', 'circa 1900') as intervals with soft bounds, propagate temporal constraints through reasoning chains, and version facts so corrections create new intervals rather than rewriting history. Quality is measured by interval accuracy on annotated temporal corpora and by contradiction-detection recall. The limits are genuinely unknown dates and narrative texts with no explicit time — those get open intervals with their uncertainty recorded, never a fabricated precision.

t: Accuracy, evaluation, and limits of the Temporal Fact Resolver
title: Accuracy, evaluation, and limits of the Temporal Fact Resolver
description: Evaluation: how the Temporal Fact Resolver is tested, where it is accurate, and where it reaches its limits. Real resolvers extract temporal expressions with parsers like SUTime or HeidelTime, normalize them to dates, and attach validity intervals [start, end) to every fact. Allen's interval algebra — thirteen relations including before, meets, overlaps, during, and equals — classifies how any two intervals relate, which detects contradictions (two CEOs 'during' the same month) and supports point-in-time queries ('who was CEO on 2020-06-01?'). Bitemporal models track both when something was true and when the archive learned it. Advanced systems handle fuzzy dates ('early 1990s', 'circa 1900') as intervals with soft bounds, propagate temporal constraints through reasoning chains, and version facts so corrections create new intervals rather than rewriting history. Quality is measured by interval accuracy on annotated temporal corpora and by contradiction-detection recall. The limits are genuinely unknown dates and narrative texts with no explicit time — those get open intervals with their uncertainty recorded, never a fabricated precision.
demo:
# Temporal Fact Resolver - runnable demo (JAH-ATK179-000012)
RANK = 3
SIG = False
FACTS = [('Version 1.0', 2015, 2017), ('Version 2.0', 2017, 2021), ('Version 3.0', 2021, None)]  # (fact, start_year, end_year or None)
def allen(a, b):
    (s1, e1), (s2, e2) = a, b
    e1 = e1 or 9999; e2 = e2 or 9999
    if e1 < s2: return "before"
    if e1 == s2: return "meets"
    if s1 < s2 < e1 < e2: return "overlaps"
    if s2 <= s1 and e1 <= e2 and (s1, e1) != (s2, e2): return "during"
    if (s1, e1) == (s2, e2): return "equals"
    if s1 == s2: return "starts"
    return "related"
print("facts on the timeline:")
for f, s, e in FACTS:
    print("  [%s-%s] %s" % (s, e or "now", f))
if RANK >= 2:
    print("interval relations:")
    for i in range(len(FACTS)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(FACTS)):
            print("  '%s' %s '%s'" % (FACTS[i][0][:25], allen(FACTS[i][1:], FACTS[j][1:]), FACTS[j][0][:25]))
if RANK >= 3:
    q = 2020
    holder = [f for f, s, e in FACTS if s <= q <= (e or 9999)]
    print("true in %d: %s" % (q, holder if holder else "nothing recorded"))
if SIG:
    print("Signature lineage stamp: JAH-SIG-TMP-" + "JAH-ATK179-000012")
print("record:", "JAH-ATK179-000012", "OK")
